root_causes.description: The shipping service exhibits a severe p99 latency spike (~4.7s vs ~2ms p50 baseline) with zero errors and no CPU/memory stress, and its only downstream dependency (quote) is clean at 1.98ms — the delay originates inside shipping itself. Checkout's p99 (~9.5s) is almost exactly 2x shipping's p99 plus ~130ms (checkout makes two sequential shipping RPCs: GetQuote and ShipOrder), and frontend's p99 (~4.8s) is 1x shipping's p99 plus ~130ms, confirming shipping as the origin of the latency propagation chain.

evidence.observed_value: p99=4684.879ms, p95=3904.396ms, p50=1.98ms, max=4880ms, anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: p99 < 5ms (p50=1.98ms in same window; shipping is a lightweight quote/ship gRPC service)
quote is shipping's only dependency and is healthy, so shipping's slow server spans are not caused downstream

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.001 cores, max=0.001 cores, no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: latency is not resource-driven (no CPU stress on shipping pods)

evidence.expected_baseline: shipping spans normally complete in ~2ms; slow-but-successful traces confirm pure latency, not failures

evidence.observed_value: Only routine event: 'Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource (count=1)'; no OOMKilled/BackOff/crash events
evidence.expected_baseline: No crash-loop or resource-pressure events for shipping pods

root_causes.description: Checkout shows the highest absolute p99 (~9.5s vs 24.85ms p50), but its latency profile is fully explained by propagation from the slow shipping dependency: checkout p95/p99/max (7924/9504/9900ms) equal 2x shipping's p95/p99/max (3904/4684/4880ms) plus a constant ~120-140ms, matching checkout's two sequential shipping RPCs. No errors, no CPU/memory stress, no restarts, and no error logs, so a checkout-local fault is the less likely alternative hypothesis.

root_causes.description: Frontend p99 rose to ~4.8s (p50 32.9ms), which is propagated latency: frontend's slow requests equal one shipping call (~4.7s) plus ~130ms overhead, and its checkout-dependent requests inherit checkout's ~9.5s. Frontend is a victim of the downstream shipping latency, not the origin.

evidence.observed_value: p99=4825.350ms, p95=4026.750ms, p50=32.875ms, max=5025ms, anomaly detected

evidence.expected_baseline: payment (another checkout dependency) is healthy, isolating the latency source to shipping

remediation_steps: Remove the latency fault injection on the shipping service: check flagd feature-flag/experiment configuration and any Chaos Mesh network-delay or app-level delay experiment targeting the shipping deployment, then roll it back.
Add strict gRPC deadlines/timeouts on checkout's calls to shipping (GetQuote and ShipOrder) and cache shipping quotes so a slow shipping dependency cannot inflate checkout and frontend p99.
Configure latency SLO alerts (e.g., shipping p99 > 500ms for 2 minutes) and circuit-breaking for repeated slow shipping calls from checkout and frontend.
After mitigation, verify recovery: shipping p99 should return to ~2ms, and checkout/frontend p99 should fall back below 100ms.
